historic/u1e3/brookes-slave-ship.jpg.description: Stowage diagram of the British slave ship Brookes under the Regulated Slave Trade Act of 1788. Iconic Middle Passage image.

historic/u1e3/cantino-planisphere.jpg.description: The Cantino planisphere (1502), Portuguese manuscript world map showing the Atlantic, Europe, Africa, and the New World. Main map for E3 MapJourney beats.

historic/u1e3/disease-dark.jpg.description: Engraving of a plague doctor (Wellcome Collection). Dark, serious tone for E3 disease-section backgrounds.

historic/u1e3/feral-pigs.jpg.description: Wild boar engraving, National Gallery of Art open access collection

historic/u1e3/florentine-codex-page.jpg.description: Nahua depiction from Book 12 of the Florentine Codex (1577): a healer (ticitl) tending smallpox sufferers in 1520. Used behind PrimarySourceSpotlight HIPP analysis.

historic/u1e3/maize-botanical.jpg.description: Leonhart Fuchs, maize illustration from De historia stirpium (1542)

historic/u1e3/potato-plant.jpg.description: 17th century Dutch watercolor of a potato plant (Solanum tuberosum), Rijksmuseum — 3372x4494

historic/u1e3/smallpox-victims.jpg.description: Nahua depiction of smallpox victims (Florentine Codex tradition). Serious tone for E3 '8 or 9 out of 10' beat.

historic/u1e3/sugarcane-plantation.jpg.description: Frans Post, Brazilian landscape with sugar mill (17th c., Dutch Brazil, Staatliches Museum Schwerin). Shows the plantation labor system for E3 labor-crisis beats.

historic/u1e3/tenochtitlan.jpg.description: 1524 Nuremberg/Cortés map of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital on the lake — 3029x1931

historic/u1e3/tomato-plant.jpg.description: Solanum lycopersicum (tomato) botanical artwork, Naturalis Biodiversity Center

historic/u1e3/wheat-field.jpg.description: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Harvesters (1565) — 16th century wheat harvest

historic/u1e4/burgesses-assembly.jpg.description: The first House of Burgesses assembly at Jamestown, 1619 (Armstrong illustration, public domain).

historic/u1e4/delaware-portrait.jpg.description: Thomas West, 3rd Baron De La Warr (Lord Delaware), 1605 portrait — governor who saved Jamestown in 1610.

historic/u1e4/james-i.jpg.description: James VI and I of England, portrait by Paul van Somer — granted the Virginia Company charter; author of A Counterblaste to Tobacco.

historic/u1e4/james-river-map.jpg.description: Captain John Smith's 1612/1624 map of Virginia, showing Chesapeake Bay and the James River — used for the three-ships MapJourney.

historic/u1e4/john-smith.jpg.description: Captain John Smith, c.1617 engraving (National Portrait Gallery, after Simon van de Passe). CC0 dedication.

historic/u1e4/pocahontas-real.jpg.description: The real Pocahontas (Matoaka/Rebecca Rolfe), 1616 engraving by Simon van de Passe — the only lifetime portrait. NOT Disney.

historic/u1e4/powhatan-village.jpg.description: The 1622 Powhatan attack on the English settlements near Jamestown — engraving in the style of Theodor de Bry (Matthäus Merian tradition).

historic/u1e4/starving-time.jpg.description: Bleak winter landscape (Bruegel, Hunters in the Snow, 1565) — dark visual for the Starving Time, winter 1609-1610.

historic/u1e4/three-ships.jpg.description: The three Jamestown replica ships (Susan Constant, Godspeed, Discovery) sailing the James River, 2007 US Navy photo.

historic/u1e4/tobacco-curing.jpg.description: Workers cutting tobacco and loading sticks for the curing/drying barn (1939 FSA/OWI photo, public domain — process shown is centuries-old, though photo is modern).

historic/u1e4/tobacco-plant.jpg.description: Nicotiana tabacum (tobacco plant) botanical illustration from Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen (1887, public domain).

historic/u1e4/virginia-company.jpg.description: Seal of the Virginia Company of London.

historic/u1e4/white-lion-ship.jpg.description: 17th-century Dutch armed merchantman/privateer by Wenceslaus Hollar (Rijksmuseum) — representative of the White Lion, the Dutch privateer that brought the first Africans to Virginia in 1619. CC0.

historic/u1e5/guaman-poma-miner.jpg.description: 1615 Guamán Poma de Ayala drawing 'Corregidor de minas' showing the cruel punishment of Indigenous mine workers (manuscript p. 529).

historic/u1e5/jean-bodin.jpg.description: 1586 title page of Jean Bodin's 'De Republica libri sex' (Six Books of the Republic), the work behind his quantity theory of money.

historic/u1e5/manila-galleon.jpg.description: 1743 painting of the Spanish galleon Nuestra Señora de Covadonga, which sailed the Manila galleon route, under capture.

historic/u1e5/mercury-patio.jpg.description: 19th-century photograph of the mercury-amalgamation patio process, with mules treading ore pulp in a walled patio.

historic/u1e5/ming-porcelain.jpg.description: Ming dynasty Chinese porcelain jar with floral decoration, the luxury good traded east for American silver.

historic/u1e5/mita-miners.jpg.description: 18th-century engraving of a cross-section of a Potosí silver mine with miners digging, climbing ladders, and hauling ore.

historic/u1e5/pacific-galleon-route.jpg.description: 1748 Anson chart of the Pacific Ocean marking the Spanish galleon's track between Manila and Acapulco.

historic/u1e5/philip-ii.jpg.description: Workshop of Titian portrait of Philip II of Spain in black with the Order of the Golden Fleece (Museo del Prado).

historic/u1e5/pieces-of-eight.jpg.description: Obverse and reverse of a Spanish colonial 8-reales silver cob coin of Philip IV, the 'piece of eight.'

historic/u1e5/pillars-hercules-coin.jpg.description: Engraving of a 1661 pillar dollar showing the Pillars of Hercules with the PLVS VLTRA banner, origin of the dollar sign.

historic/u1e5/potosi-cerro-rico.jpg.description: The conical Cerro Rico silver mountain looming over the rooftops of Potosí, Bolivia.

historic/u1e5/potosi-city-view.jpg.description: 16th-century woodcut 'Cerro del Potosí' showing the city at the foot of the silver mountain.

historic/u1e5/potosi-mint.jpg.description: Historic photograph of the Casa de la Moneda (royal mint) building in Potosí.

historic/u1e5/silver-ingots.jpg.description: 1897 photograph of stacked silver bullion bars in a vault.

historic/u1e5/toledo-viceroy.jpg.description: Colonial portrait of Francisco de Toledo, Viceroy of Peru, who organized the mita labor system.

historic/u1e6/anaquito-battle.jpg.description: Labeled sketch 'Batalla del Campo de Anaquito' — the 1546 battle where Gonzalo Pizarro's encomendero rebels defeated Viceroy Blasco Núñez Vela. (554px wide, under the 800px target; the only PD depiction of the battle found.)

historic/u1e6/casta-painting.jpg.description: 18th-century Mexican casta series — 16 labeled panels (e.g. 'Español con India, Mestizo') classifying mixed-race families.

historic/u1e6/debt-peonage.jpg.description: 1910 photograph from John Kenneth Turner's 'Barbarous Mexico' — hundreds of laborers lined up at a Yucatán henequen plantation under a mounted overseer; the classic image of debt peonage.

historic/u1e6/encomienda-workers.jpg.description: 1615 Guamán Poma de Ayala drawing 'Encomendero y familia andina' — a Spanish encomendero with the Andean family under his authority. (Substitution: depicts the encomendero with his charges rather than overseen workers; 651px wide.)

historic/u1e6/hacienda.jpg.description: 19th-century engraving of the hacienda at Uxmal, Yucatán (after Désiré Charnay, 'Ancient Cities of the New World', 1887) — the colonial estate house at the heart of the hacienda system.

historic/u1e6/las-casas.jpg.description: 1886 oil portrait of Bartolomé de Las Casas, Dominican friar and defender of Indigenous rights.

historic/u1e6/middle-passage-ship.jpg.description: The 1789 Brookes slave-ship diagram ('Description of a Slave Ship', British Library) — cross-section and deck plans showing enslaved Africans packed for the Middle Passage.

historic/u1e6/new-laws.jpg.description: Title page of the 1542 Leyes Nuevas ('New Laws') — 'Leyes y ordenanças... para la governacion de las Indias y buen tratamiento y conseruacion de los Indios' — with the imperial arms of Charles V.

historic/u1e6/repartimiento-draft.jpg.description: 1615 Guamán Poma de Ayala drawing (Nueva corónica, p.535) — an Indigenous captain interfacing with a Spanish miner holding ore; the mita/repartimiento draft was organized through Native officials for the mines. (Substitution: no PD Commons image depicts the draft itself; sourced from the Royal Danish Library like E5's Poma drawing; 381px wide.)

historic/u1e6/sao-tome-sugar.jpg.description: Frans Post, 'Engenho de açúcar' (c. 1664) — a Brazilian sugar mill (engenho) with workers. (Substitution: no PD São Tomé-specific image found; the Brazilian engenho is the same plantation-mill complex pioneered on São Tomé.)

historic/u1e6/silver-mine-workers.jpg.description: Theodor de Bry engraving (c. 1590, after José de Acosta) — Indigenous workers climbing ladders and laboring in the Potosí silver mines. Distinct from E5's four Potosí images; intended as the E5 callback.

historic/u1e6/sugar-cane-cutting.jpg.description: William Clark, 'Slaves cutting the sugar cane' (1823), plate IV of 'Ten Views in the Island of Antigua' (British Library) — enslaved workers harvesting cane under an overseer on horseback.

u1e7/las-casas-portrait.jpg.description: Anonymous 16th-century portrait of Bartolomé de las Casas (1474-1566) in Dominican habit, writing with a quill

u1e7/sepulveda-portrait.jpg.description: Portrait engraving of Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda (1490-1573) by José Maea, from Retratos de españoles ilustres

u1e7/valladolid-1550.jpg.description: Braun & Hogenberg, 'Vallisoletum' — panoramic view of Valladolid, Spain, from Civitates Orbis Terrarum, 16th century

u1e7/aristotle-bust.jpg.description: Roman marble bust of Aristotle (restored head on ancient bust), Capitoline Museums

u1e7/aquinas-portrait.jpg.description: Engraved portrait of Thomas Aquinas ('Divus Thomas de Aquino'), Rijksmuseum RP-P-OB-105.257

u1e7/short-account-title.jpg.description: Title page of Brevísima relación de la destrucción de las Indias, Seville 1552, by Bartolomé de las Casas

u1e7/charles-v-titian.jpg.description: Titian, Portrait of Charles V Seated, 1548 (MDXLVIII)

u1e7/new-laws-document.jpg.description: Title page of the Leyes Nuevas (New Laws of the Indies, 1542) — 1585 Madrid printing by Francisco Sánchez (page 7 of bound volume)

u1e7/black-legend-press.jpg.description: Stradanus (Jan van der Straet), printers at work in a 16th-century workshop — preparatory drawing for Nova Reperta, c. 1590

u1e7/dominican-friar.jpg.description: Workshop of Peter Paul Rubens, portrait of a Dominican friar (Las Casas's order)

u1e7/spanish-court-1550.jpg.description: Engraving of Charles V's abdication in favour of Philip II before the imperial court at Brussels, 25 Oct 1555 (A. van der Does; Rijksmuseum)

u1e7/oviedo-chronicle.jpg.description: Title page of Gonzalo Fernández de Oviedo's Sumario de la natural historia de las Indias, Toledo 1526

u1e8/santa-fe-1680.jpg.description: Dana B. Chase, 1880s albumen photograph of the Palace of the Governors, Santa Fe — the colonial seat besieged in the 1680 revolt; 5093x3440

u1e8/pope-statue.jpg.description: Edward S. Curtis, 'Wyemah' — portrait of a Taos (Tewa) elder, 1905; representative image, no contemporary portrait of Popé exists; 2834x3780

u1e8/knotted-cord.jpg.description: Knotted fiber cord (quipu), plate from 'The Ancient Quipu' — Popé's signal for the coordinated 1680 uprising was a knotted maguey-fiber cord; 2421x1847

u1e8/maguey-plant.jpg.description: 18th-century botanical engraving of agave ('Aloe Americana,' pre-Linnaean) — maguey fiber made the cords carried by Popé's runners; 2000x3000

u1e8/franciscan-mission.jpg.description: Mission San Xavier del Bac, Tucson, ca.1900 (CHS-800) — a Franciscan mission church of the Spanish Southwest; 4804x3662

u1e8/kiva-interior.jpg.description: NPS photograph of an excavated kiva interior — circular ceremonial chamber with bench, hearth and sipapu; 7970x5343

u1e8/pueblo-village.jpg.description: 19th-century photograph of Taos Pueblo — multi-story adobe village with ladders, residents and hornos beneath the mountains; 4392x2856 (Library of Congress)

u1e8/spanish-soldier-1600s.jpg.description: Jacob de Gheyn II, plate 40 from Wapenhandelinghe (1607) — a matchlock musketeer of the type Spain fielded in 17th-century New Mexico; 2681x3732 (CC0 via the Met)

u1e8/otermin-retreat.jpg.description: Loren Mozley, 'Pueblo Revolt 1680' — 1936 Treasury Relief Art Project mural (US federal work) in the Albuquerque courthouse; Pueblo warriors with torches and bows drive out Spanish soldiers and settlers; 4845x1159 (editorial crop of wall fixtures)

u1e8/vargas-reconquest.jpg.description: Diego de Vargas's 1692 inscription — 'Aqui estuvo el Genl Dn Diego de Vargas... Año de 1692' — claiming the reconquest of New Mexico, with English translation; 1626x825

u1e8/new-mexico-map.jpg.description: Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, 'Plano Geografico' of New Mexico, 1778 — Spanish manuscript map of Nuevo México; 1303x961

u1e8/trevino-governor.jpg.description: Period engraving of Don Luis de Requesens, a 16th-century Spanish governor — representative portrait, no portrait of Governor Treviño survives; 1200x1526

u1e8/yucca-plant.jpg.description: Yucca gloriosa, hand-colored plate from Curtis's Botanical Magazine, vol. 31 (1810); 3754x3092

u1e8/desert-runners.jpg.description: Edward S. Curtis, 'The Vanishing Race — Navaho' (1904) — riders crossing the desert at dusk; evokes the runners who carried Popé's knotted cords; 5242x4246
